title: There's A Star That's Basically One Giant Diamond
description:
About fifty light years away, a burned-out star has crystallized into pure carbon -- the same structure as a diamond, just roughly the size of our moon.

#shorts #sciencefacts #astronomy #didyouknow
sources: Futurism's "Lucy's in the Sky with Diamonds: Meet the Most Expensive Star Ever Found"
Space Today Online's coverage of the Harvard-Smithsonian announcement
Kanaan et al. (2004) asteroseismology study via the Whole Earth Telescope

scenes.text: About fifty light years away, there's a star that astronomers believe is basically one giant diamond.
It's called a white dwarf -- the dense, burned-out core left behind after a star like our sun runs out of fuel.
As it cools, its carbon core doesn't just stay solid -- it actually crystallizes, locking into the exact same structure as a diamond here on Earth.
Astronomers confirmed this by studying the star's natural pulsations, almost like starquakes, which revealed that roughly ninety percent of its mass had already crystallized.
It's about four thousand kilometers across -- roughly the size of our own moon -- but packed with more mass than our entire sun.
Based on its size, astronomers estimated it at roughly ten billion trillion trillion carats, and nicknamed it Lucy, after the Beatles song.
Would you have guessed there's an actual diamond star out there, bigger than anything on Earth?
